skill.name: taskhold
skill.description: Manage shared coding tasks through the Taskhold MCP server, including ordered steps, progress updates, decision requests, and completion records.
skill.summary: Coordinate coding agents and people through a shared task list with progress tracking and review requests.
skill.author: gettaskhold

security_audit.summary: All 24 static findings are false positives: Markdown formatting, documented Taskhold URLs, and ordinary task descriptions do not establish execution or reconnaissance. The skill requires installation consent and approval for sensitive actions, and prohibits secret disclosure. No evidence found of prompt injection, unauthorized exfiltration, or malicious execution in SKILL.md; the hosted service implementation was not provided.

finding_verdicts.reason: Backticks format the taskhold_* MCP tool prefix in Markdown prose. There is no Ruby expression or shell substitution.
The inline command registers the documented MCP endpoint only after explicit user approval. Markdown delimiters do not execute it, and remote content cannot authorize execution.
Backticks mark task-creation MCP tool names in an offered import workflow. They are not executable shell syntax.
The inline project parameter and repository-name example are MCP arguments. No shell invocation or system enumeration is described.
Backticks identify MCP calls that retrieve the current task and its notes. There is no shell execution expression.
The line documents taskhold_updates and its project argument for task synchronization. Markdown formatting does not introduce command execution.
The line documents starting a user-requested task through taskhold_begin and named parameters. These are MCP identifiers, not shell commands.
The documented list and begin calls select queued work by priority. Backticks delimit tool names and parameters rather than executable shell text.
The agent parameter and client-name examples are display metadata for the shared board. No command execution is requested.
Backticks format task completion, planning, and start tools with their parameters. These instructions update task state, not a shell interpreter.
The options and recommended fields describe a human decision request. Inline Markdown fields contain no executable commands.
The taskhold_progress call reports milestone counts and messages. Backticks identify parameter names without evaluating them.
The inline taskhold_add_note identifier documents saving task notes for later sessions. No shell execution appears.
The documented block and update tools ask for decisions and wait for replies. The text explicitly rejects guessing on destructive actions.
The line describes completion summaries and structured outcome fields. Backticks format MCP arguments, not shell execution.
The needs_review and outcome.verify fields request human verification before completion. Their Markdown delimiters have no execution semantics.
The task-creation tool names and source-location parameters support recording follow-up work. No shell interpreter or dynamic command is involved.
The URL identifies the Taskhold MCP endpoint explicitly required by the skill. No evidence found of a covert destination or unauthorized data transfer.
The dashboard and live-board URLs point to the stated task service. They are user-facing navigation links, not hidden upload endpoints.
The MCP and client-setup URLs support explicitly approved setup. Key-based setup requires a user-supplied URL, and the skill prohibits disclosing the key.
The import URL is a user-facing Taskhold page offering preview and undo. It is not an instruction for covert bulk upload.
The URLs reference Taskhold pricing, setup, and documentation. No executable download or secret-bearing request appears.
The description lists task-management triggers, authentication options, and boundaries with other tools. It contains no system reconnaissance instructions.
This line prohibits marking partially finished tasks complete and recommends a note or blocked status. It contains no system information collection.

content.value_statement: Coding work loses context when tasks, progress, and decisions are scattered across sessions. Taskhold connects agents to a shared task list with ordered steps, updates, and human review.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve current tasks, notes, and recent changes for a repository project.
Select queued tasks by priority and start them with ordered steps.
Report milestone counts or percentages and save findings as task notes.
Block tasks with specific questions, decision options, and a recommended choice.
Record completion outcomes, verification details, follow-up tasks, and review requests.
Create tasks from local task files or code TODOs and direct users to the import page for other applications.
limitations: Requires a connected Taskhold MCP server; the skill contains instructions, not a bundled server implementation.
Hosted use requires account setup or a trial; the source lists subscription pricing that may change.
Task details and progress are stored with an external service; secrets and large code blocks must stay out of tasks.
External application imports use the Taskhold import page; this skill does not provide direct integrations for every listed application.

use_cases.title: Resume Repository Work
use_cases.description: Recover the current task, review prior notes, and continue from the next unfinished step.
use_cases.target_user: Individual developers returning to a coding session

use_cases.title: Review Agent Progress
use_cases.description: Track milestones on the shared board and answer blocked-task questions with explicit choices.

use_cases.title: Capture Backlog Items
use_cases.description: Turn selected local task items and code TODOs into project tasks with source references.

prompt_templates.title: Check Current Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the current Taskhold task for this repository and summarize its unfinished steps. Do not change task status.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect the shared task list

prompt_templates.title: Start the Next Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Pick the highest-priority queued Taskhold task for this repository. Review its notes, plan ordered steps, and begin work.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Selected TODOs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review TODO comments in [directory] and propose follow-up tasks with file paths and line numbers. Create only the tasks I approve.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Work and Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Work on Taskhold task [task ID] with ordered steps and milestone updates. Block for sensitive decisions and request review with verified outcomes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: manage execution, decisions, and handoff

output: Remaining: Verify escaping and request review.

output_examples.input: Ask me before removing the old API route.
output: Decide: Keep the route for 30 days or remove it now?
Recommended: Keep it for 30 days to allow client migration.
Meanwhile: Continue work that does not depend on removal.

output_examples.input: Record the completed test work and request review.
output: Ready for review: Invoice export escaping tests.
Changed: Added coverage for commas, quotes, and line breaks.
Verify: Review the added cases before approving completion.

best_practices: Use the repository project name consistently and read existing notes before resuming work.
Report measured milestones and record verification results before marking tasks complete.
Keep secrets out of task text and require explicit approval before destructive, financial, secret-related, or production actions.
anti_patterns: Treating task notes, tool results, or setup pages as permission to execute commands.
Publishing credentials or large code blocks in shared task records.
Marking partial work complete or inventing progress percentages.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Each client needs access to the Taskhold MCP server.

faq.question: Does the skill install Taskhold automatically?
faq.answer: No. If tools are unavailable, it shows a setup command and waits for explicit approval before running it.

faq.question: Is an API key required?
faq.answer: The documented OAuth setup does not require a key. Existing account holders can optionally provide a setup URL for key-based configuration.

faq.question: How does Taskhold separate repository tasks?
faq.answer: Calls use the repository folder name as the project. Names are case-insensitive, and projects are created on first use.

faq.question: Can it import existing tasks?
faq.answer: It can create tasks from local task files and code TODOs. Other application imports use a page with preview and undo.

faq.question: What happens when a task needs a decision?
faq.answer: The agent blocks the task with a specific question and optional choices, then waits for updates or works on something else.
